# Exercise 02-1

# À propos de pi

pi is $\pi$

```{r}
cat("the value of π ->", pi, "\n")
```

[Aiguilles de Buffon](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aiguille_de_Buffon)
```{r}
N <- 1000000
x <- runif(N, min = 0, max = 1)
theta <- runif(N, min = 0, max = pi / 2)
2 / (sum((x + sin(theta)) > 1) / N)
```
```{r}
mu <- 100
sigma <- 15
x <- mu + sigma * rnorm(10000)
hist(x, breaks = 40)
grid()
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Variables
#   N     : number of needles thrown (here 1,000,000)
#   x     : distance from the centre of the needle to the nearest line
#   theta : angle between the needle and the parallel lines
#   mu    : mean of the normal distribution used for the plot
#   sigma : standard deviation of that normal distribution
#
# Functions
#   runif(n, min, max) = "random uniform"
#     Draws n random numbers uniformly between min and max
#     (every value has the same chance). runif(N) == runif(N, 0, 1).
#
#   rnorm(n, mean, sd) = "random normal"
#     Draws n random numbers from a bell-shaped normal distribution
#     with mean `mean` and standard deviation `sd`.
#
#   sum()   : here counts how many TRUE there are
#   sin()   : sine, applied to the whole vector at once (vectorisation)
```
